newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Evacuation plans halted in northern Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Evacuation plans halted in northern Cambodia.

text.p: A plan to evacuate a group of foreign tourists and aid workers from the northern town of Siem Reap was scrapped on Tuesday because of fighting between forces loyal to the country's rival prime ministers.

A Western source in Siem Reap, near Cambodia's famed Angkor Wat ruins, said the tourists and aid workers -- who had expected to travel overland to the Thai border, about 150 km (90 miles) to the west -- were in a state of confusion in the town.
A British tourist who spoke to Reuters from Siem Reap late on Monday was nervous about the fighting and had hoped to leave with his family in a convoy to Aranyaprathet in eastern Thailand.
But the Western source said travel was not possible because of fighting near the town and landmines on the road between Siem Reap and the Thai border.
"There's fighting outside the city and a lot of troop movements," the source said.

The source said the town itself was quiet on Tuesday morning but fighting had broken out overnight when forces loyal to ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh were withdrawing from Siem Reap to join comrades in nearby countryside.
"Last night, the remaining FUNCINPEC forces were able to extricate themselves from the town after a two-day standoff," he said, referring to Ranariddh's men. FUNCINPEC is Ranariddh's royalist party.
Five soldiers loyal to powerful Second Prime Minister Hun Sen had been wounded in the fighting, the source said, quoting a military official loyal to Hun Sen.
Siem Reap town was under the control of forces loyal to Hun Sen while large areas of the surrounding countryside were under the control of forces loyal to Ranariddh.
Fighting between the two camps broke out in the capital on Saturday and Hun Sen took control of Phnom Penh by Monday morning.

Two large groups of foreigners, totalling about 100, fled across the border over the past two days. Both groups were made up mostly of aid workers and were led in a convoy from Battambang in western Cambodia to Aranyaprathet by the Australian defence attache.
Phnom Penh's international airport has been closed since Saturday morning because of the fighting.
Two Thai military transport planes arrived in the capital on Tuesday to evacuate Thai and other nationals trapped by the fighting, witnesses said.
